subject: Hosted integration deep-dive — scheduling and prep
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@medlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted integration deep-dive — proposed times and agenda

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. Per our conversation, we'd love to run a technical deep-dive focused on your engineering team's integration with Redwood Hosted API: SDK usage, streaming responses, and tool/function calling (webhook examples).

Proposed 60–75 minute slots (PDT):
- Mon Nov 1 — 10:00–11:15am
- Tue Nov 2 — 9:00–10:15am
- Wed Nov 3 — 1:00–2:15pm

Agenda (attached):
- 10’ intros + goals
- 20’ architecture & integration patterns (SDKs + streaming)
- 20’ function/tool calling and webhook examples
- 15’ Q&A + next steps / mutual action plan

Attachments: [Attachment: deep-dive-agenda.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

If you can confirm a slot and attendees, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short pre-call checklist for the engineers. Also looping Marissa (solutions) and Rishi (runtime) to help with any deep technical asks.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@medlytics.com>

Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted integration deep-dive — proposed times and agenda

Camila —

Thanks, appreciate the clear agenda. Laura and a couple of our platform engineers (one focused on streaming) want to join. Unfortunately we have a conflict on Mon Nov 1 at 10am. Can we move to Tue Nov 2 at 9am PT?

Also: could you include a short example that shows a streaming response with token-level metadata and a quick function-calling flow that hits an external webhook? Those are key for our compliance review.

Participants from our side:
- Sam Patel (PM)
- Dr. Laura Chen (Head of Platform)
- Miguel Torres (Platform Engineer)

Thanks — Sam
Sam Patel
Product Lead, Integrations
MedLytics

Tue Nov 2 at 9:00am PT works great. I’ll send the calendar invite (attached .ics) and a short pre-call checklist for your engineers.

Quick prep notes for your team: please bring:
- A short architecture diagram (1 slide) showing where the inference calls will be made and where webhooks land
- Any existing SDK usage or proxy layers (node/python/go versions)
- Typical concurrency/throughput expectations and peak QPS

We’ll make sure the walkthrough includes:
- Streaming example with token-level metadata and how we expose it in the SDK
- Function/tool calling with an example external webhook and retry/backoff patterns
- Recommendations for batching/caching to hit your latency/cost targets

Camila / Rishi —

Thanks for the heads up. Quick notes from prep side before we lock the invite:
- Rishi, please prepare a 10’ slide that shows the streaming SDK surface (node + python examples) and one small code snippet that demonstrates token metadata in the stream payload.
- Include a small function-calling example showing an outbound webhook and the recommended verification/secret pattern (HMAC).
- Add a one-minute slide about batching + KV cache benefits (numbers vs. no-cache) — Miguel will likely push on throughput/cost.

Camila: can you confirm whether MedLytics requires signed attestations for data residency during the demo? If yes, we should have Stephanie prep the SOC2 snapshot and a short note about private deployment options.

I drafted a couple of slides and added them to the prep doc.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Two quick asks for the session:
